Summary: Exploitation of internet-facing component (Contact center platform)
Description: Internet-facing components are continuously scanned and attacked. Unpatched vulnerabilities or injection flaws can give an attacker a foothold.

Summary: Weak or missing user authentication (Contact center platform)
Description: Users reach this entry point. Without strong authentication, an attacker can impersonate a user with stolen or guessed credentials.

Summary: Denial of service on internet-facing component (Contact center platform)
Description: Traffic floods or abusive clients can make the service unavailable.

Summary: Direct prompt injection and jailbreaks (Amazon Bedrock)
Description: Users can craft prompts that override the system's instructions or safety rules.

Summary: Sensitive information disclosure through the model (Amazon Bedrock)
Description: Prompts and responses can contain PII or confidential data, whether typed by users or pulled in from retrieval.

Summary: Excessive agency (Amazon Bedrock)
Description: The AI can take actions (call APIs, change data, send messages). A manipulated or mistaken model can do real damage with whatever tools and permissions it has.

Summary: Model output trusted by downstream systems (Amazon Bedrock)
Description: If model output is rendered in a browser or passed to code, SQL, or APIs without validation, it can cause XSS, injection, or unintended actions.

Summary: Unknown sensitive data in storage (Call transcripts (S3))
Description: Teams often store more sensitive data than they realize (e.g. PII in documents or exports). Without scanning, it isn't protected or classified correctly.

Summary: Sensitive data written to logs (Logs (CloudWatch → SIEM))
Description: Logs often capture request bodies, tokens, or AI prompts. They are usually readable by more people than the source data.

Summary: Unencrypted data flow (F5: Account lookup API → Core banking system)
Target: F5: Account lookup API → Core banking system
Description: Data on this flow can be read or modified by anyone positioned on the network path.

Summary: Sensitive data sent to a third party (F1: Customer (caller) → Contact center platform)
Description: Sensitive data leaves our environment for a vendor. We depend on the vendor's controls and contract for its protection.

Summary: Privileged / admin access without strong controls (Contact Center IVR Assistant)
Description: Administrators or support staff have elevated access. Compromise of one admin account can expose the whole application and its data.

Summary: Long-lived static credentials in workloads (Account lookup API)
Description: Workloads that use static keys or passwords can have them leaked through code, images, logs, or environment variables, and the keys keep working until someone rotates them.

Summary: Long-lived static credentials in workloads (IVR orchestrator (Lambda))
Description: Workloads that use static keys or passwords can have them leaked through code, images, logs, or environment variables, and the keys keep working until someone rotates them.

Summary: Over-privileged workload identity (Account lookup API)
Description: If the workload's role has broader permissions than it needs, any compromise of the workload becomes a compromise of everything that role can reach.

Summary: Broken object-level authorization (Account lookup API)
Description: Users may be able to read or change records that belong to other users by changing an ID in a request (a top API risk).

Summary: Data store reachable from public networks (Call transcripts (S3))
Description: Managed data and AI services often have public endpoints by default. A misconfigured policy can expose data to the internet.

Summary: Card data captured in AI prompts or logs (Amazon Bedrock)
Description: If card numbers reach model prompts, transcripts, or logs, those systems come into PCI scope and must meet all its controls.

Summary: Card data captured in AI prompts or logs (Logs (CloudWatch → SIEM))
Description: If card numbers reach model prompts, transcripts, or logs, those systems come into PCI scope and must meet all its controls.

Summary: Unbounded consumption and cost abuse (Amazon Bedrock)
Description: Heavy or abusive use can run up large costs or exhaust quotas for everyone.

Summary: System prompt leakage (Amazon Bedrock)
Description: Attackers can often extract the system prompt. Secrets or access rules placed in it will be exposed.

Summary: Single point of failure for a critical application (Account lookup API)
Description: A critical application depends on a component that may not survive a zone failure.

Summary: Data destruction or ransomware (Call transcripts (S3))
Description: An attacker or mistake could delete or encrypt the data. Without protected backups, recovery may be impossible.

Summary: Sensitive data sent to a third party (F5: Account lookup API → Core banking system)
Target: F5: Account lookup API → Core banking system
Description: Sensitive data leaves our environment for a vendor. We depend on the vendor's controls and contract for its protection.

Summary: Sensitive data sent to a third party (F6: IVR orchestrator (Lambda) → Payment processor)
Description: Sensitive data leaves our environment for a vendor. We depend on the vendor's controls and contract for its protection.

Summary: Logs can be altered or disabled (Logs (CloudWatch → SIEM))
Description: An attacker with enough access may delete logs or turn logging off to hide activity.

Summary: Uncontrolled outbound traffic enables data exfiltration (Account lookup API)
Description: If the workload can reach any destination on the internet, an attacker who compromises it can send sensitive data out or download tools.

Summary: Uncontrolled outbound traffic enables data exfiltration (IVR orchestrator (Lambda))
Description: If the workload can reach any destination on the internet, an attacker who compromises it can send sensitive data out or download tools.

Summary: Event injection into serverless function (IVR orchestrator (Lambda))
Description: Functions triggered by events (queues, storage, HTTP) may trust event data. Malicious input can lead to injection or abuse of the function's permissions.

Summary: Vendor or SaaS handling sensitive data (Core banking system)
Description: A vendor stores or processes our sensitive data. A breach on their side is a breach of our customers' data.

Summary: Vendor or SaaS handling sensitive data (Payment processor)
Description: A vendor stores or processes our sensitive data. A breach on their side is a breach of our customers' data.
